geometry_edits.rationale: Strengthen the access-side carve so it reads as a public entry condition on the verified frontage edge.
Make the void deeper and more legible while preserving the hall as the dominant mass.
Improve section_program_fit by giving the hall a clearer folded roof expression associated with span/daylight.
Preserve the long-span alignment of the hall body.

graph_edits.rationale: Widen the access-side subtraction so the west-facing threshold becomes a clearer public seam in plan and elevation.
Deepen the notch enough to register as occupied entry/court space rather than a minor chip.
Shift the roof/section from a shallow shed toward a more gym-appropriate folded profile that better expresses span and daylight without changing the dominant mass.
Keep the long-span logic aligned with the observed long axis so the hall remains the dominant program body.

rationale: The candidate reads as one compact low-rise mass with a clear primary body, so it can plausibly support the gymnasium brief, but the open-space figure is only moderately legible and the access response is still somewhat muted relative to the verified frontage. Across the four views the form is coherent, with no obvious view-to-view collisions, but the stepped terrace language is weakly programmatic rather than strongly hall-based. The profiled-hall roof exists, which helps section fit, yet the section is still fairly shallow and not especially expressive of span/daylight. The west-facing notch/open edge is the right kind of gesture for the access side, but it should read more clearly as a public threshold or entry seam rather than a minor subtraction. Compared with the references, it resonates most with the low horizontal sports pavilion lineage, especially the combination of dominant hall plus subordinate edge condition, but it remains more box-derived than the strongest precedents.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low horizontal sports-pavilion massing with a clear canopy-like roof gesture and attached subordinate volume; useful as a precedent for keeping one dominant hall legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More fragmented than the candidate; do not copy the dispersed composition if the current mass needs a single dominant hall.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Dispersed low pavilions and courtyard-like gaps can support a sports program when the dominant mass stays calm and the open space reads as circulation/public realm.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is more rectilinear and stepped; avoid over-faceting just to imitate the reference.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Faceted low-rise massing with a noticeable cutout/opening and skylight-like roof articulation suggests a way to introduce daylight and public entry without losing compactness.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference leans more open and perimeter-based; the candidate still needs its access-side void to be clearer across views.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A long horizontal pavilion with a legible perimeter opening/courtyard edge is useful for calibrating the access response and public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Its peaked/cantilevered roof is a different section language; do not copy the silhouette literally.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single dominant hall-like roof profile over a low base with a subordinate appendage is transferable for maintaining program hierarchy.

warnings: The visible roof/section is acceptable for a compact training hall, but it is not yet strong enough to imply a large-span civic gymnasium.
The stepped massing is coherent but close to generic terrace layering; avoid over-reading it as a meaningful inhabited section unless it gains clearer ground/void consequence.
